target.name: American Housing Corporation
target.founder: Bobby Fijan, Riley Meik, Harris Rothaermel, William Davis

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Pre-Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $200K total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
American Housing Corporation is a pre-seed stage venture in the Housing & Construction sector founded by Bobby Fijan, Riley Meik, Harris Rothaermel, and William Davis. The company has raised $200K to date. No comparable public or private peer companies were available for direct multiple-based valuation.

Given the limited data and absence of a robust comp universe, valuation relies on stage-progression methodology. Using the $200K in total raised as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of pre-seed to seed-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $500K. This reflects the expected value accretion associated with progression to the next financing stage, absent product-market fit signals or material operational metrics.

The triangulation range of $425K to $575K (median $500K) is narrow and reflects reliance on a single applicable method. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue, user traction, or defensible IP data; lack of housing and construction sector comparables; and the inherent volatility of pre-seed valuations. Any investment thesis should be grounded in founder background, product progress since the initial $200K raise, and capital efficiency to date. A more robust valuation would require either peer transaction data from the housing-construction space or material operational progress milestones.
